answer_1.quote: Automatically generating textual descriptions from structured data improves the accessibility of knowledge bases to lay users. Such applications include explaining data records to non-experts , writing sports news , summarizing information in multiple documents , and generating dialogue responses .
answer_1.outputs: natural language descriptions from structured data

answer_2.quote: We use a variety of automatic metrics and human evaluation (Section 4) to evaluate the quality of the generated text. We report BLEU, METEOR, and TER which are used in the official WebNLG challenge. However, these measures have limitations in considering the semantic meanings of words or phrases , therefore we also report MoverScore , BERTScore , and BLEURT  that incorporate semantics rather than surface forms using contextual embeddings. Furthermore, we include PARENT  which explicitly aligns n-grams from the reference and generated text to the data contents.

answer_4.quote: We ask 5 internal annotators to evaluate on 100 triplesets sampled from declarative sentence partition and another 100 triplesets sampled from human written sentence partition.
answer_4.guideline: We defined three levels of fluency: fluent, mostly fluent, and not fluent, and the same for semantic faithfulness.
